track_a.rationale: Framed glazed door and windows are fitted with frames, sashes and sills, still covered in JAKO-branded protective film.
Walls are bare cast-in-place concrete. Formwork panel joints, tie marks and blotchy stains are visible everywhere, with no plaster coat.
Several red-capped flush boxes are set into the concrete walls near floor level, with conduits running to them.
Floor is a rough bare slab. Electrical conduits lie loose on its surface and would be buried if screed had been laid.
White window frames with sashes and sills, still covered in protective JAKO film, are fitted in the brick external wall.
The external wall shows bare red clay blockwork around the windows with no internal plaster. Only the corner beads are fixed.
The bare concrete slab ceiling is clearly visible throughout, with only small holes. There is no ventilation ductwork anywhere.
Internal door opening in the left concrete wall is empty, with no leaf or frame hung; the corridor beyond is clearly visible.
Every window opening has white framed units fitted with sashes and sills. Protective film with JAKO labels is still on them.
Bare cast concrete slab soffit covers the whole room, with precast panel joints and recessed box holes visible.
Walls clearly visible: bare brick and concrete with flush socket boxes. Red pipe stubs with brass fittings look like plumbing. No surface conduit drops seen.
Ceiling is clearly visible bare concrete slab with panel joints and no suspended grid, hangers or tiles anywhere.
Right and front walls look plastered, but the left walls are bare formed concrete and the back corner pier is unplastered.
The floor is bare, dusty screed/concrete with debris on it. There are no tiles or parquet anywhere in view.
The wall under every window is clearly visible and bare. Only pipe stubs come out at floor level; no radiators are mounted.
Ceiling_front shows an open, unclosed rectangular opening in the concrete slab. More small open ceiling cut-outs are near the right/back wall.
The ceiling is clearly visible bare concrete with only small holes and openings. No sprinkler pipes, drops or heads are anywhere.
The back walls show bare concrete with patchy grey render around a window. No waterproofing membrane is visible, and the windows suggest it isn't a basement.
Stair walls have rough grey speckled render with patchy marks and no paint finish visible; the ceiling above is bare concrete.
The whole stair flight and both side walls are clearly visible. No handrail, brackets or balustrade appear anywhere along the stair.
Dark conduits run in cut chases in plastered/blockwork walls: column between front windows, beside right doorway, and left corridor wall.
Front room has framed window/door units with sashes and sills (glass dropped out); framed window visible at end of right corridor.
Smooth, uniform screed surface across floors with blue perimeter edge strips at wall bases, typical of poured floating screed.
Vertical and horizontal chases with dark conduit laid in them, plus back-box holes, on the bed wall, the pier between the windows and beside the door.
The walls are plastered, but the chases are still open with the conduit exposed, so they have not been plastered over.
The floor is clearly visible and shows finished screed with blue edge strips. No underfloor heating pipes are visible anywhere.
Two white sanitary carrier frames are mounted on the stud wall, with red supply pipework and fittings connected at the base.
The front wall has metal studs with board on the far face only. The left partitions are boarded, so boarding has started.
The sloped roof shows exposed Würth membrane, timber battens and rafters throughout. No plasterboard covers the roof insulation.
The carrier frames are bare and only pipe stubs are visible. No WC pans or basins are mounted on them.
Full-height white-framed doors with sashes stand on the exterior walls. Glass mostly drops out in the scan, but the frames and fixings are plainly installed.
The partition doorway in the left view is an empty opening with no door leaf or hinges visible. The other partition opening is also open with no leaf.
Every wall is clearly visible and shows only bare render with loose cable conduits and back boxes. No distribution board enclosure appears anywhere.
Ceiling is clearly visible bare formed concrete soffit throughout; only small wall-top hangers/brackets, no ductwork runs anywhere.
Bundles of long metal track/profile sections lie on timber bearers on the slab in front of the scanner.
Slab is widely visible as bare grey concrete with no painted bay lines; the only white item is a small loose-looking object.
Several silver galvanized conduit runs and a tray fixed to the concrete soffit cross the ceiling in the front view.
The opening between levels holds only a temporary scaffold stair tower; no permanent stair or balustrade is visible.
The floor is not clean: debris, hoses, wet-looking patches and an open pit with a loose plank, so it isn't ready for coating.
Timber-framed windows with sashes and sills are fitted all along the facade window line; glass partly drops out but the frames are installed.
Wrapped window units on a rack, framed glazed units leaning on walls, and loose glass panels sit on the floor.
Internal walls with door openings are built on the back side, and stud framing shows through the doorways.
Continuous concrete floor with blue chalk setting-out lines, but a poured screed can't be told apart from a power-floated structural slab here.
Opening in the concrete core wall is closed off with black sheeting, steel props and a red timber edge rail.
Soffit is clearly visible bare concrete everywhere. Only one red pipe stub hangs down; no sprinkler heads anywhere.
Galvanised metal studs and tracks stand in front of the concrete walls, with no plasterboard fixed anywhere.
Blue WC carrier frames with cisterns stand along the wall. A red vertical riser drain with branches and supply pipes is clamped in place.
The WC area is clearly visible but has only bare carrier frames and studs. There are no cubicle partitions, pans or basins.
Elevation enclosed by thin timber batten grid with sheeting and a diagonally braced timber door, which looks like a temporary weather enclosure, not a permanent facade.
Red double-rail guardrails on steel posts run along the exposed mezzanine slab edges overhead and at the opening at the back.
The front wall is boarded and screw-fixed. On the left, purple boards are fixed between metal studs, so boarding has started.
A large stack of purple boards, which look like plasterboard, sits on the concrete slab right of the scanner. More stacked boards are visible further back.
The boarded wall shows bare joints and exposed screw heads with no tape or filler. The left partition is studs with boards between them, not ready for decoration.
The concrete core doorways are empty openings with no door leaves. The stair opening has only a temporary OSB hoarding door, not a fitted leaf.
Plastic sheeting fixed to timber battens covers the perimeter facade openings on several sides.
The ceiling is clearly visible bare concrete soffit with formwork joints. There are no radiant ceiling panels anywhere.
Spiral ventilation ducts with branches hang from the concrete soffit; services and cabling are fixed along it. Dedicated cable tray is less distinct.
Front partition is plasterboard with white jointing compound over the seams and screw heads, so jointing is in progress.
Full-height glazed facade units with frames, mullions and fixing brackets are installed along the outer wall.
The bare concrete soffit is clearly visible with exposed services. There is no suspended ceiling grid or tiles anywhere.
The corridor soffit has a perforated cable tray, conduit runs, a spiral duct, rectangular ductwork and a white pipe, all hung on rods.
The red door frames are empty, with open stud rooms visible through them. No leafs are hung, and unfitted frame sections lie on the floor.
The corridor floor is bare screed with debris scattered on it. No carpet has been laid anywhere in view.
Pipework is visible on the soffit, but a scan can't show whether it has been pressure-tested or charged.
Ceiling is newly boarded, but only the joints and screw spots are filled; the board face is bare, so it has not been skim-plastered.
Door casings and frames are wrapped in clear plastic film, held with blue and yellow tape, on several doorways.
The walls show bare brick with old mortar all round the room; there is no new plaster coat.
Black corrugated cable conduits run down vertical wall chases to red back boxes on the brick walls.
Several round back-boxes with red caps are set into the bare brick walls, with conduit drops running to them on the right and left walls.
A white-framed window with sashes is visible on the front wall, but the scan cannot show whether it is a new replacement unit.
The walls are bare brick and the conduits in the chases are still exposed; no plaster covers the chases on any visible wall.
Several recessed ceiling boxes with loose cable tails hanging down are visible across the concrete soffit.
Openings have no door leaf, frame or hinges. Left opening shows only rough timber boarding; right opening is open and bright.
Walls are bare blockwork with visible joints and raw concrete with formwork marks. No skim plaster anywhere.
Two open ceiling penetrations with rough exposed edges are clearly visible, not closed or made good.
